### Triangle

The class template [`Triangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html "Closed triangle stored by three vertices.") is stored as three points, called vertices, which are kept in the following order. The first vertex is the smallest lexicographically and the other two vertices are ordered such that the triangle is oriented counterclockwise (positive orientation test). Two triangles are equal if they have the same vertices.

```C++
pgl::Triangle t(3,3,4,1,1,1);
std::cout << t << std::endl;
// Output: <(1,1)(4,1)(3,3)>
for(size_t i : {0,1,2}) std::cout << t[i] << ' ';
// Output: (1,1) (4,1) (3,3)
for(pgl::Point p : t) std::cout << p << ' ';
// Output: (1,1) (4,1) (3,3)
for(pgl::Segment s : t.edges()) std::cout << s << ' ';
// Output: (1,1)--(4,1) (3,3)--(4,1) (1,1)--(3,3)
for(pgl::OrientedSegment s : t.orientedEdges()) std::cout << s << ' ';
// Output: (1,1)->(4,1) (4,1)->(3,3) (3,3)->(1,1)
```

A triangle `t` has methods such as:

- [`t.isDegenerate()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#ab159614e587f6dc4a75789f98fb7a848 "Tests whether the three vertices are collinear."): Returns true if there are equal vertices or all vertices are collinear.
- [`t.isPoint()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#a3243eca48511601f01fb32091485c278 "Returns whether the triangle collapses to a single point.") / [`t.getIfPoint()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#ac5aefd4a3e5dc47f3b72c54a5549aae5 "Returns the point the triangle collapses to, if it does."): Whether the triangle collapses to a single point (all defining points equal), and that point as a `std::optional<PointType>`.
- [`t.isSegment()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#a89a15128d0219b2fafea898c6be83503 "Returns whether the triangle collapses to a non-degenerate segment.") / [`t.getIfSegment()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#aa3b1c560fe887b46423db140976e3ffd "Returns the segment the triangle collapses to, if it does."): Whether the triangle collapses to a segment of positive length (defining points collinear but not all equal), and that segment as a `std::optional<Segment>`.
- [`t.isUndefined()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#a21a0527077026023a860af4502fa36a9 "Returns whether the triangle is degenerate without collapsing to a point or to a segment."): Always `false`: a degenerate triangle is always a point or a segment.
- `t.centroid<ResultNumber>()`: Returns the centroid.
- [`t.circumcircle()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#a0b9e50f4c10a634c4706884ff2894fb7 "Returns the circumcircle of the triangle."): Returns the circumcircle.
- [`t.isRectangle()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#a4cfb7d8fffa11293343c535bc4825e3f "Tests whether the triangle has a right angle."): Returns whether one angle is 90 degrees.
- [`t.isObtuse()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#a7848d637384e479a97395489bf9a61fb "Tests whether the triangle has an obtuse angle."): Returns whether one angle is greater than 90 degrees.
- [`t.isIsosceles()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#a3cc30d928e1cb21c99eae9765f38e3d4 "Tests whether two sides have the same length."): Returns whether two sides have the same length.

It knows how to convert itself to:
- `(pgl::Polygon) t` or [`t.asPolygon()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#aaa078dd16798d8d58bb3cb46f64aba3b "Returns the triangle as a simple polygon."): Returns the polygon representation of the triangle.
- `(pgl::Convex) t` or [`t.asConvex()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#ab01b4c98a0859edd28f1961012ff1447 "Returns the triangle as a convex polygon."): Returns the convex polygon representation of the triangle.
- [`t.asPolygonWithHoles()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#abe42baab6be8b188613e10bda0b5866f "Returns the triangle as a hole-free region."): Returns the triangle as a hole-free [`PolygonWithHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html "Closed region bounded by one outer simple polygon minus disjoint polygonal holes.") region.

- Other methods: [`a`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#a49e6b3ba0db01d986087b842b54d9131 "Returns the first vertex."), ### Rectangle

The class template [`Rectangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html "Axis-aligned rectangle stored by minimum and maximum corners.") represents an axis-aligned rectangle. While it is stored internally as only two vertices (minimum and maximum x and y coordinates), it behaves as a polygon with four vertices. It can be constructed for any number of points in a container and will construct the bounding box rectangle. If only two points are given, the container is optional. If the two points are respectively the minimum x and y and the maximum x and y, then an optional argument set to true avoids the bounding box calculation.

A default-constructed rectangle is **empty**: it stores the corners `(0,0)` and `(-1,-1)`, so its maximum falls below its minimum and it covers no point. Normalizing two opposite corners never reaches that state, so it is produced only by `Rectangle()`, by the `minmax` constructor given inverted corners (which normalizes any such pair to the one canonical empty value), and by the operations that answer with a rectangle covering nothing — the bounding box of an empty range or of an empty shape, for instance. Inserting into an empty rectangle does not grow those placeholder corners: [`r.insert(p)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#a02c20ec22014c7dbd29d3b2489527b59 "Enlarges the rectangle so that it contains the given point.") makes `r` the single point `p`.

```C++
pgl::Rectangle r({{1,3},{2,4},{3,1},{5,4},{2,3}});
// Same as pgl::Rectangle r({1,1},{5,4}) or pgl::Rectangle r({1,4},{5,1});
std::cout << r << std::endl;
// Output: [(1,1),(5,4)]
std::cout << r.min() << ' ' << r.max() << std::endl;
// Output: (1,1) (5,4)
for(size_t i : {0,1,2,3}) std::cout << r[i] << ' ';
// Output: (1,1) (5,1) (5,4) (1,4)
for(pgl::Point p : r) std::cout << p << ' ';
// Output: (1,1) (5,1) (5,4) (1,4)
for(pgl::Segment s : r.edges()) std::cout << s << ' ';
// Output: (1,1)--(5,1) (5,1)--(5,4) (1,4)--(5,4) (1,1)--(1,4)
for(pgl::OrientedSegment s : r.orientedEdges()) std::cout << s << ' ';
// Output: (1,1)->(5,1) (5,1)->(5,4) (5,4)->(1,4) (1,4)->(1,1)
```

A rectangle `r` has methods such as:

- [`r.empty()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#a657019a958bfe05f096961a1982f4df6 "Returns whether the rectangle is the empty set of points."): Returns true if the rectangle covers no point, that is, if its stored maximum corner falls below its minimum one on either axis. An empty rectangle behaves as [`EmptyShape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1EmptyShape.html "The empty set of points in the plane.") everywhere: [`r.size()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#aca9d8fcb8ecdd1ed85414d298b5a3b11 "Returns the number of corners: 4, or 0 when empty.") is `0`, iteration over its corners and edges yields nothing, [`r.area()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#a2edf35e30a352a900730b7531dfc9d22 "Returns the rectangle area.") is `0`, and reading `r[i]`, [`r.vertices()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#a8e890106e82852c58aaa51ceff095275 "Returns the four vertices in counterclockwise order."), [`r.edges()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#a7017ee8e082661250fdcdf9948033f71 "Returns the four edges as unordered segments."), [`r.centroid()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#a553634d0d486ae85ec22c6a036855f0e "Returns the centroid of the rectangle."), or [`r.circumcircle()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#a96f720c89b9116686118e6085374a7ab "Returns the circumcircle of the rectangle.") is a precondition violation.
- [`r.isDegenerate()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#a380388f13b2cd9a5ad8f4f806e31be84 "Returns whether the rectangle has empty interior."): Returns true if the rectangle has null area, which includes the empty one.
- [`r.isPoint()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#a2a7b0a353e1de16f126d4f2c05724b17 "Returns whether the rectangle collapses to a single point.") / [`r.getIfPoint()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#a03286af73bd9f2e39b2cd41116ac6182 "Returns the point the rectangle collapses to, if it does."): Whether the rectangle collapses to a single point (all defining points equal), and that point as a `std::optional<PointType>`.
- [`r.isSegment()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#a726c28bd48ef2d27e5230785a4305972 "Returns whether the rectangle collapses to a non-degenerate segment.") / [`r.getIfSegment()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#af1c975c7dbb89ed3dcd607720b13fb08 "Returns the segment the rectangle collapses to, if it does."): Whether the rectangle collapses to a segment of positive length (defining points collinear but not all equal), and that segment as a `std::optional<Segment>`.
- [`r.isUndefined()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#ab64d082aacdbab58a7b0f2b1b1c18445 "Returns whether the rectangle is degenerate without collapsing to a point or to a segment."): Always `false`: a degenerate rectangle is always empty, a point, or a segment.
- `r.centroid<ResultNumber>()`: Returns the centroid.
- [`r.circumcircle()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#a96f720c89b9116686118e6085374a7ab "Returns the circumcircle of the rectangle."): Returns the circumcircle.
- [`r.insert(s)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#a02c20ec22014c7dbd29d3b2489527b59 "Enlarges the rectangle so that it contains the given point."): Enlarges the rectangle in order to contain a finite shape `s`. The shape must expose [`bbox()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#ae88798364c0bf20cd4d14c259fa33dcd "Returns the bounding box of the rectangle.").
- [`r.insert(points)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#a02c20ec22014c7dbd29d3b2489527b59 "Enlarges the rectangle so that it contains the given point."): Enlarges the rectangle in order to contain every point in the input range.

It knows how to convert itself to:
- `(pgl::Polygon) r` or [`r.asPolygon()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#af850885808c25c90aaa04506cc1f1537 "Returns the rectangle as a simple polygon."): Returns the polygon representation of the rectangle; an empty rectangle gives the empty polygon.
- `(pgl::Convex) r` or [`r.asConvex()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#a9c20bb08763579e119ea85d68a907ab3 "Returns the rectangle as a convex polygon."): Returns the convex polygon representation of the rectangle; an empty rectangle gives the empty convex polygon.
- [`r.asPolygonWithHoles()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#a69f3bbc94ce41e98cf2271c573d4b42e "Returns the rectangle as a hole-free region."): Returns the rectangle as a hole-free [`PolygonWithHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html "Closed region bounded by one outer simple polygon minus disjoint polygonal holes.") region.

### Disk

The class template [`Disk`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html "Closed Euclidean disk stored by boundary points plus optional disk label.") represents a circle with its interior. Disks are stored internally as three boundary points, in the same way as a [`Triangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html "Closed triangle stored by three vertices."). This choice may be surprising, as the standard representation for disks is a center point and a radius. The main motivation is that the circumcircle of a triangle may be represented exactly for integers. Nevertheless, the constructor accepts both forms:

```C++
pgl::Disk d1({1,1}, {2,5}, {4,3}); // Disk from 3 points
pgl::Disk d2({2,3}, 4);            // Disk from a point and a radius
std::cout << d2 << std::endl;
// Output: Disk((-2,3)(6,3)(2,7))  // Output always uses 3 points
```

Disk does not have the [`intersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#a21e0cb8c11c045cddeccbe886d46ea86 "Returns the intersection of the two shapes (A ∩ B), re-dispatching through the wrapper's own intersection.") method and cannot be scaled on a single axis. A disk `d` has methods such as:

- [`d.isDegenerate()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#a19e32c8b7656bfe02982c8a40ea0ff57 "Returns whether the three boundary points are collinear."): Returns true if the points are collinear or equal.
- [`d.isPoint()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#ae60c11c6b7ab1819ec87492a5fb78714 "Returns whether the disk collapses to a single point.") / [`d.getIfPoint()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#a0f9d7c74a8feb3b7806eb7c6b972a9fc "Returns the point the disk collapses to, if it does."): Whether the disk collapses to a single point (all defining points equal), and that point as a `std::optional<PointType>`.
- [`d.isUndefined()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#ac9d870ebc7f49459d33602a03843a54a "Returns whether the disk is degenerate without collapsing to a point."): True if the boundary points are collinear but not all equal, so they do not determine a circle (three distinct collinear points have no circle through them; two distinct ones have infinitely many). A disk is never a segment, so this and [`isPoint`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#ae60c11c6b7ab1819ec87492a5fb78714 "Returns whether the disk collapses to a single point.") cover every degenerate disk.
- `d.radius<ResultNumber = double>()`: Returns the radius length. A radius can be irrational, so the result is floating-point by default. Notice that when the disk is defined by center and radius, we may set `ResultNumber` to the same number type as the defining point.
- `d.squaredRadius<ResultNumber>()`: Returns  the squared radius.
- `d.center<ResultNumber>()`: Returns the center point.
- `d.diameter<ResultNumber>()`: Returns a diameter [`Segment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html "Unoriented closed segment between two endpoints plus optional segment label."). A center/radius disk uses its stored horizontal diameter; a genuine three-point disk uses one boundary point and its reflection across the center.
- `d.minkowskiSum<ResultNumber = double>(e)`: Returns the [Minkowski sum](shape_methods.md#minkowski-sum) of two disks, which is a [`Disk`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html "Closed Euclidean disk stored by boundary points plus optional disk label."): the centers add and so do the radii. This is the one curved sum the library can answer, and the one sum that is not exact by default — each radius is a square root of what a disk stores — which is why the result type defaults to `double` here as it does on [`radius`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#a69765084e501902a81583032fdb7c816 "Returns the center in this disk's exact coordinate type."). Two center/radius disks carry both quantities exactly, so their sum with an exact `ResultNumber` is exact. A disk sums with a [`Point`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html "Two-dimensional point with optional label payload.") (a translation) and with nothing else: a disk and a segment sweep out a stadium, which is not a shape here.

- Other methods: [`a`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#aab80a3c4810748f39fdc8c7e020eb232 "Returns the first boundary point (lexicographically smallest)."), [`area`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#aa4f2837f14655fd73098513f769e41da "Returns the squared radius in this disk's exact result type."), [`b`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#aeb247fff089ba4d4463418f84f0f9e3d "Returns the second boundary point in canonical order."), [`bbox`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#a82543add1cf92f0b0116fd798ddecced "Returns an axis-aligned bounding box in the coordinate type."), [`begin`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#aaec2b4934b1b89530f0ea126a080f4ef "Returns an iterator to the first boundary point."), [`boundaryContains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#a190ee43500b52f235991dc9bc3095180 "Tests whether this shape's boundary contains the other shape (∂A ⊇ B)."), [`c`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#a20d60679286b84a64063b648c860430e "Returns the third boundary point in canonical order."), [`cbegin`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#ad39c1b05f308f292112590c388575a36 "Returns a const iterator to the first boundary point."), [`cend`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#a5c10cddfceeff5a571f4b892ba2e11ad "Returns a const iterator past the last boundary point."), [`center`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#a01f21dd5b971164474843df4ad71bfc1 "Returns the center (circumcenter of the three boundary points) in an explicitly chosen coordinate type."), [`contains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#a40627a86d5eb68250e7daba7a1ca36db "Tests whether this shape contains the other shape (A ⊇ B)."), [`crosses`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#a3afd10decc72c4a11747024bee9c635b "Tests whether the two shapes mutually separate each other (each disconnects the other)."), [`diameter`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#ad7c86ba7778cf349bcb6c653e0470ba5 "Returns a segment defining a diameter of the disk."), [`distanceL1`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#a88d634c92f9daedd726c8e72724cacd9 "Returns the Manhattan (L1) distance from this disk to a point."), [`distanceLInf`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#a629a2dbfcbe9013da2a5191095ef0ab1 "Returns the Chebyshev (LInf) distance from this disk to a point."), end."), [`index`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#ab6e63f207efba3178e1a665c70f60cd0 "Returns the smallest index i with (*this)[i] == point, or -1 if no boundary point equals point."), [`interiorContains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#a5c43e8fa09ae818be5fa70d2f18c9474 "Tests whether this shape's interior contains the other shape (A∖∂A ⊇ B)."), [`intersects`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#a04a545293c1496c34b4bf601a124eff6 "Tests whether this shape and the other shape intersect (A ∩ B ≠ ∅)."), [`pointInside`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#a78477a3bcf69c6f36cff63e5a65442e3 "Returns the midpoint of the first two boundary points."), interior of shape."), [`rotate90`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#a8d38ec21e40e6459475c0006646d352b "Rotates the disk by 90k degrees around the origin in place."), [`squaredRadius`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#a0027c4ab0d85b7ff3e5b0d5b42b1745f "Returns the squared radius in an explicitly chosen result type.").


### Monotone Chain

The class template [`MonotoneChain`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html "Weakly x-monotone polyline stored by lexicographically sorted vertices.") represents an x-monotone polyline: a polyline whose vertices are strictly increasing in the lexicographic order (smaller x first, breaking ties by smaller y). A chain with $n$ vertices has $n-1$ edges and no closing edge, so it is an open curve and is automatically simple. Its boundary is its two extreme vertices and its interior is everything else.

A chain may be constructed from any container of points, which will be sorted automatically and duplicates removed. The input is treated as a point set, not as a pre-linked chain, so any permutation of the same points yields the same chain. If the points are already sorted and unique, a second parameter true can be given to avoid sorting the points again.

We use the term above to refer to larger y coordinates and below to refer to smaller y coordinates. A chain `P` with $n$ vertices has methods such as:

- [`P.isDegenerate()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a7eb13f8c59d5d0798e3e15bfca4739a6 "Checks if the chain is degenerate (fewer than two vertices, so it has no edge)."): Returns true if the chain has fewer than two vertices, and hence no edge.
- [`P.isPoint()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a708590c0009a716028fae8035d4a54f5 "Checks whether the chain covers exactly one point.") / [`P.getIfPoint()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#aed62d933eb36ec518a6b0c687f44535c "Returns the point the chain collapses to, if it does."): Whether the chain collapses to a single point (all defining points equal), and that point as a `std::optional<PointType>`.
- [`P.isSegment()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a52154db7e279b99081a8f353f152c5e6 "Checks whether the chain covers exactly one segment of positive length.") / [`P.getIfSegment()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#ac602a20992a726b74a86eddde2808374 "Returns the segment the chain collapses to, if it does."): Whether the chain collapses to a segment of positive length (defining points collinear but not all equal), and that segment as a `std::optional<Segment>`.
- [`P.isUndefined()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#af4cf40049c2bcc7e75d18f14986c80a7 "Checks whether the chain is degenerate without covering a point or a segment."): True only for an empty chain, which has no vertex.
- [`P.isStrictlyMonotone()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#ad6166871233a0625fdd3ce18f00b2f5c "Tests whether the chain is strictly x-monotone."): Returns true if no two vertices share an x-coordinate, so the chain is the graph of a function of x. Takes $O(n)$ time.
- [`P.insert(p)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a5cd1ec77da22ad3d957149d51e3d8a05 "Extends the chain to contain the given point as a vertex."): Extends the chain in order to contain another point `p` as a vertex.
- [`P.insert(points)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a5cd1ec77da22ad3d957149d51e3d8a05 "Extends the chain to contain the given point as a vertex."): Extends the chain in order to contain all the given points as vertices.
- [`P.erase(p)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a376349e07c8783ff501fbfb4865937b8 "Removes the vertex at the given index (in lexicographic order).") / [`P.erase(i)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a376349e07c8783ff501fbfb4865937b8 "Removes the vertex at the given index (in lexicographic order)."): Removes a vertex, given as a point or by its index in the lexicographic order (as in `P[i]`), the first returning whether it was a vertex (found in $O(\log n)$ comparisons, since the vertices are sorted) and the second requiring `i` to be smaller than [`P.size()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a65249728c15a81dcc9732202c1e7cf46 "Returns the number of vertices in the chain."). Erasing an interior vertex reroutes the chain through a single edge between its neighbors, and erasing an extreme vertex shortens the chain.
- [`P.indexAtX(x)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a393d5b3cc782e79a7036ee3beb72257f "Locates the vertex or edge of the chain at a given x-coordinate."): Returns an `std::optional<size_t>` that is engaged if the chain contains a point of x-coordinate `x`. The returned value is the smallest index `i` such that `P[i].x() == x`, or the unique `i` with `P[i].x() < x < P[i+1].x()`. Takes $O(\log n)$ time.
- `P.yAtX<ResultNumber>(x)`: Returns an `std::optional` with the y coordinate at `x` (at a vertical edge, the y of the edge's bottom vertex). Takes $O(\log n)$ time. Interpolation may divide, so integral receivers widen to ERational by default.
- [`P.isBelow(p)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a4bc4bcb2b9210d4d4d320556798ee343 "Tests whether the chain passes weakly below a point."): Returns an `std::optional<size_t>` that is engaged if a ray shot down from `p` intersects `P`; the value is the index [`indexAtX`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a393d5b3cc782e79a7036ee3beb72257f "Locates the vertex or edge of the chain at a given x-coordinate.") returns for `p.x()`. Takes $O(\log n)$ time, exactly.
- [`P.isAbove(p)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a9eaf22f78515682edac8b3b1590615f1 "Tests whether the chain passes weakly above a point."): The same for a ray shot up from `p`. Note that [`isBelow`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a4bc4bcb2b9210d4d4d320556798ee343 "Tests whether the chain passes weakly below a point.") and [`isAbove`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a9eaf22f78515682edac8b3b1590615f1 "Tests whether the chain passes weakly above a point.") are not complementary: both are engaged when `p` lies on the chain.
- [`P.length()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#aeeb80f55a73ab440b6e119e02827ee74 "Computes the Euclidean length of the chain (the sum of its edge lengths)."), [`P.lengthL1()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#afca60f5968fff4ff8e6a1d8c38aeeaa3 "Computes the Manhattan (L1) length of the chain."), [`P.lengthLInf()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a6b0f1704432d4fff888a8cd935a499f9 "Computes the Chebyshev (LInf) length of the chain."): Return the Euclidean, Manhattan, and Chebyshev lengths of the chain.

The monotone structure speeds up several predicates and constructions:

- [`P.contains(s)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a5ca0039a7ceff302c988f0ee2fca3226 "Tests whether this shape contains the other shape (A ⊇ B).") takes $O(\log n)$ time if `s` is a point, and $O(\log n + k)$ if `s` is a segment whose x-range spans $k$ vertices (a chain contains a segment exactly when the segment is a straight sub-path of the chain).
- [`P.intersects(s)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a3ff7a150d0eff57b3538d5375c299cec "Tests whether this shape and the other shape intersect (A ∩ B ≠ ∅).") takes $O(\log n + k)$ time for a segment overlapping $k$ edges of the chain.
- [`P.intersects(P2)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a3ff7a150d0eff57b3538d5375c299cec "Tests whether this shape and the other shape intersect (A ∩ B ≠ ∅).") and [`P.intersection(P2)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#acf0c387012c4d665ac17e0c3fecec81b "Returns the intersection of the two shapes (A ∩ B), empty when they are disjoint.") take $O(n+m)$ time if `P2` is a chain with $m$ vertices, via a merge sweep over the two sorted vertex sequences. [`P.intersection(s)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#acf0c387012c4d665ac17e0c3fecec81b "Returns the intersection of the two shapes (A ∩ B), empty when they are disjoint.") returns an `std::vector` of points and segments sorted by the lexicographic order, with collinear overlaps coalesced; the same form is returned for segments, lines, rays, halfplanes, rectangles, triangles, and convex polygons.
- [`P.edgesCross(P2)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a45e24dfac70758449ba7139d2b04c956 "Tests whether the two chains have edges that cross."): Returns true if `P` has a point strictly above `P2` and a point strictly below it, i.e. every sufficiently small perturbation of the vertices of `P` and `P2` still yields intersecting chains. Unlike [`P.crosses(P2)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#ac70944fe81641ed674b8a30e44f246c1 "Tests whether the two shapes mutually separate each other (each disconnects the other)."), a touch that does not swap sides never counts. The x-extents of `P` and `P2` must overlap in more than a single point, or the result is false outright — a shared x that is only one chain's own extreme vertex (e.g. a chain that is a single vertical edge) is not robust to perturbation. Takes $O(n \log m + m \log n)$ time if `P2` has $m$ vertices.
- `P.minkowskiSum<ResultNumber>(b)`: Returns a [`Polygon`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html "Closed simple polygon stored by its vertices.") when `b` is a [`Triangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html "Closed triangle stored by three vertices."), [`Rectangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html "Axis-aligned rectangle stored by minimum and maximum corners.") or [`Convex`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html "Closed convex polygon stored by its vertices."). A monotone chain is the one non-convex shape whose Minkowski sum with a nondegenerate convex one is always a single polygon and needs no arrangement, although a boundary-piece crossing can still produce a rational vertex. A flat operand is off that contract — its sum can pinch shut, which no simple polygon may — and belongs to the region-valued [`Segment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html "Unoriented closed segment between two endpoints plus optional segment label.") overload. See [Minkowski Sum](shape_methods.md#minkowski-sum).


### Polyline

The class template [`Polyline`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html "Open polygonal chain stored in traversal order; may self-intersect.") represents a polyline, also called a polygonal chain, polygonal curve, polygonal path, or piecewise linear curve. Unlike [`MonotoneChain`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html "Weakly x-monotone polyline stored by lexicographically sorted vertices."), the order of the vertices matter and the polyline is allowed to self-intersect. A polyline with $n$ vertices has $n-1$ edges and no closing edge. Its boundary is its two extreme vertices and its interior is everything else.
A polyline can be constructed from any container of points, or from a flat list of coordinates.

A polyline `P` with $n$ vertices has methods such as:

- [`P.isDegenerate()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#a3c7ecb999d35c0430c7ec57468f9d9d1 "Checks if the polyline is degenerate (all vertices are equal, so it covers at most a single point)."): Returns true if all vertices are equal (in particular for an empty or single-vertex polyline).
- [`P.isPoint()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#af18f972ba265e25f2630d8045ab3da58 "Checks whether the polyline covers exactly one point.") / [`P.getIfPoint()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#ad1f13e3b3174f5c0d1f565208ff027d7 "Returns the point the polyline collapses to, if it does."): Whether the polyline collapses to a single point (all defining points equal), and that point as a `std::optional<PointType>`.
- [`P.isSegment()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#a036e42835c8414f8155436d31f34a228 "Checks whether the polyline covers exactly one segment of positive length.") / [`P.getIfSegment()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#ab97ebeac24bc2ec5e354fda6386c2726 "Returns the segment the polyline collapses to, if it does."): Whether the polyline collapses to a segment of positive length (defining points collinear but not all equal), and that segment as a `std::optional<Segment>`.
- [`P.isUndefined()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#a66ce19ec40fb4f2f589fadb930e66bda "Checks whether the polyline is degenerate without covering a point or a segment."): True only for an empty polyline, which has no vertex.
- [`P.isSimple()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#a109775a30d3c17acb2b610e5139a17ee "Tests whether the polyline is simple (it does not touch or cross itself)."): Returns true if the edges only intersect at the shared endpoints of consecutive edges. In an open chain the first and last edges are not consecutive, so a closed polyline (first vertex equal to the last) is not simple. Takes $O(n \log n)$ time for exact coordinate types (and $O(n^2)$ for floating point).
- [`P.length()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#a9317b71453005525d3e6d20309478119 "Computes the Euclidean length of the polyline (the sum of its edge lengths)."), [`P.lengthL1()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#aa07788cbfbca38496e4920d9a6cbc827 "Computes the Manhattan (L1) length of the polyline."), [`P.lengthLInf()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#a6a8eb393f3ee27522fc9de7d3601475a "Computes the Chebyshev (LInf) length of the polyline."): Return the Euclidean, Manhattan, and Chebyshev lengths of the polyline. A self-overlapping polyline counts every traversal of a repeated part.

Since a self-intersecting polyline has no monotone structure to exploit, the predicates scan the edges: they take $O(n)$ time against a point or a segment (segment containment takes $O(n \log n)$, as a segment may be covered by several non-consecutive collinear edges) and $O(nm)$ time against another polyline with $m$ vertices. The cut predicates use set semantics: [`separates`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#a2732dc06ae36d3f65d3f6b554bd02e76 "Tests whether removing this shape disconnects the other shape (B∖A is disconnected).") joins the surviving pieces through self-crossings and revisited vertices, so removing one point never disconnects a closed polyline. Against a two-dimensional region (halfplane, rectangle, triangle, disk, convex, or polygon), [`separates`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#a2732dc06ae36d3f65d3f6b554bd02e76 "Tests whether removing this shape disconnects the other shape (B∖A is disconnected).") searches the polyline's self-intersection arrangement (built exactly, in $O(n^2)$ pairwise edge intersections) for a cycle through the region's interior, so it also detects a pocket sealed by a loop that never touches the region's boundary.

[`P.intersection(s)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#a615fbb18098d3774821bd2b932203c02 "Returns the intersection of the two shapes (A ∩ B), empty when they are disjoint.") returns an `std::vector` of points and segments sorted by the lexicographic order, in the same form as [`MonotoneChain`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html "Weakly x-monotone polyline stored by lexicographically sorted vertices."), for segments, lines, rays, halfplanes, rectangles, triangles, convex polygons, monotone chains, and other polylines. Pieces are maximal even though a self-intersecting polyline may report them out of traversal order: collinear touching overlaps are merged (also when they come from non-consecutive edges) and points covered by a reported segment are dropped. It takes $O(n)$ segment intersections against a single shape and $O(nm)$ against a chain or polyline with $m$ vertices, plus a coalescing step quadratic in the number of pieces.


- Other methods: [`bbox`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#a0f6e26a628acedb87aada9fb34159c89 "Computes the bounding box of the polyline."), [`begin`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#a7fc2ac2f29533e0e0ae85817c58041d4 "Returns a constant iterator to the first vertex."), [`crosses`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#aebb135e0f5c547fe7f5706cdca8d93a1 "Tests whether the two shapes mutually separate each other (each disconnects the other)."), [`distanceL1`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#ad11916b51735271db1644e7aed3269bc "Returns the Manhattan (L1) distance to the given shape."), [`distanceLInf`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#a06f8935547ebe27b5d33c270c5f80c94 "Returns the Chebyshev (LInf) distance to the given shape."), ### Convex

The class template [`Convex`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html "Closed convex polygon stored by its vertices.") represents a convex polygon. It can be constructed for any number of points in a container and will construct the convex hull. The vertices are stored in counterclockwise order starting from the minimum vertex (minimum x, breaking ties by minimum y). If the container already has the vertices in order, a second constructor parameter can be set to true to avoid computing the convex hull.

A convex polygon `c` has methods such as:

- [`c.isDegenerate()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a460c2cbe73f75e60d0153be2acb1662d "Checks if the convex polygon is degenerate (has zero area)."): Returns true if the convex polygon has null area.
- [`c.isPoint()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#aa75ba1e2ad3fcb890bc56a9ef61b3af5 "Returns whether the convex polygon collapses to a single point.") / [`c.getIfPoint()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a204115d0bc10845560dc465808c3515f "Returns the point the convex polygon collapses to, if it does."): Whether the polygon collapses to a single point (all defining points equal), and that point as a `std::optional<PointType>`.
- [`c.isSegment()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a932b379d00291ec476d6c550862d9b3b "Returns whether the convex polygon collapses to a non-degenerate segment.") / [`c.getIfSegment()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#aa04d4043c4d57a12d293772e0e03d2da "Returns the segment the convex polygon collapses to, if it does."): Whether the polygon collapses to a segment of positive length (defining points collinear but not all equal), and that segment as a `std::optional<Segment>`.
- [`c.empty()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a1d297d1fd6b7c5865c0976546d6bae54 "Returns whether the convex polygon is the empty set of points."): True only for a convex polygon with no vertex, which is the empty set of points: the default-constructed one, the hull of no points, and every convex-valued result that comes back empty.
- [`c.isUndefined()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#aacb35b40818b7b0700a600a09ba57e57 "Returns whether the convex polygon is degenerate without collapsing to a point or to a segment."): Always `false`: a degenerate convex polygon is always empty, a point, or a segment.
- `c.centroid<ResultNumber>()`: Returns the centroid.
- [`c.insert(s)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a573355b49f7a15907cd3dec3ac3e8624 "Enlarges the convex polygon so that it contains the given point."): Enlarges the convex polygon in order to contain a finite shape `s`. The shape must expose its vertices.
- [`c.insert(points)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a573355b49f7a15907cd3dec3ac3e8624 "Enlarges the convex polygon so that it contains the given point."): Enlarges the convex polygon in order to contain every point in the input range.
- [`c.upperHull()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a34084131cdb827a1cf75bdc56e0018de "Returns the upper hull: the boundary chain running from the lexicographically smallest vertex to the lexicographically largest one, clockwise (above the polygon)."): Returns the upper monotone chain.
- [`c.lowerHull()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a08a0bfcddc1960c1f8ca2f5906730fdf "Returns the lower hull: the boundary chain running from the lexicographically smallest vertex to the lexicographically largest one, counterclockwise (below the polygon)."): Returns the lower monotone chain.

It knows how to convert itself to:
- `(pgl::Polygon) c` or [`c.asPolygon()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#ab08ccc569a03b8056db708b1f4e26e2f "Returns the convex polygon as a simple polygon."): Returns the polygon representation of the convex polygon.
- [`c.asPolygonWithHoles()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a521e736039189d13085ec1e0f846d937 "Returns the convex polygon as a hole-free region."): Returns the convex polygon as a hole-free [`PolygonWithHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html "Closed region bounded by one outer simple polygon minus disjoint polygonal holes.") region.

If the convex polygon `c` has $n$ vertices, then:

- [`c.diameter()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#ad44a3c0e434930328c723fcae6c4c7c9 "Returns a segment realizing the diameter (the farthest vertex pair).") takes $O(n)$ time.
- [`c.intersects(s)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a0717c549a9515d6c65cf68e620361239 "Tests whether this shape and the other shape intersect (A ∩ B ≠ ∅).") takes $O(\log n)$ time if `s` is a shape with $O(1)$ vertices (not including Disk).
- [`s.intersects(c)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a0717c549a9515d6c65cf68e620361239 "Tests whether this shape and the other shape intersect (A ∩ B ≠ ∅).") takes $O(\log n)$ time if `s` is a shape with $O(1)$ vertices (not including Disk).
- [`c.intersects(c2)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a0717c549a9515d6c65cf68e620361239 "Tests whether this shape and the other shape intersect (A ∩ B ≠ ∅).") takes $O(\min(n+m) \log(n+m))$ time if `c2` is a convex polygon with $m$ vertices.
- Other predicates take the same time as [`intersects`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a0717c549a9515d6c65cf68e620361239 "Tests whether this shape and the other shape intersect (A ∩ B ≠ ∅).").
- [`c.intersection(c2)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a755f580e0d762c88e0079bce779537ab "Returns the intersection of the two shapes (A ∩ B), re-dispatching through the wrapper's own intersection.") takes $O((n+m) log (n+m))$ time if `c2` is a convex polygon with $m$ vertices.

### Polygon

The class template [`Polygon`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html "Closed simple polygon stored by its vertices.") represents a simple polygon. It can be constructed for any number of points in a container that must be given in the order they appear on the polygon. The vertices are accessed in counterclockwise order starting from the minimum vertex (minimum x, breaking ties by minimum y).

A polygon `P` has methods such as:

- [`P.isDegenerate()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#af1d297b10aee661458543c2f5fa00645 "Checks if the polygon is degenerate (has zero area)."): Returns true if the polygon has null area.
- [`P.isPoint()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a64d2a264a8cf7368886fa822b0c6f5c2 "Checks whether the polygon covers exactly one point.") / [`P.getIfPoint()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a13b63085fa8305a445debb019fba9b63 "Returns the point the polygon collapses to, if it does."): Whether the polygon collapses to a single point (all defining points equal), and that point as a `std::optional<PointType>`.
- [`P.isSegment()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a7d86301f7c50d6e5225dcdf735029984 "Checks whether the polygon covers exactly one segment of positive length.") / [`P.getIfSegment()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a4ef69ca243d92b8147f59c5be98682be "Returns the segment the polygon collapses to, if it does."): Whether the polygon collapses to a segment of positive length (defining points collinear but not all equal), and that segment as a `std::optional<Segment>`.
- [`P.empty()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#af47294488e6bbe647f6e39d0f3f0200c "Returns whether the polygon is the empty set of points."): True only for a polygon with no vertex, which is the empty set of points.
- [`P.isUndefined()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a47467427e9ff9bb160523a5b58ff9747 "Checks whether the polygon is degenerate without covering a point or a segment."): True if the polygon is degenerate yet covers more than a segment, that is, when its zero area comes from a self-overlapping boundary rather than from collinear vertices. The empty polygon is *not* undefined; use [`empty`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#af47294488e6bbe647f6e39d0f3f0200c "Returns whether the polygon is the empty set of points.") for it.
- [`P.isSimple()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a5e182cf106f6be5ed3fb49c07daf80c6 "Tests whether the polygon is simple (its boundary does not touch or cross itself)."): Returns true if the edges only intersect at the endpoints of consecutive edges. Takes $O(n \log n)$ time for $n$ edges.
- [`P.isConvex()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a4fd2d656a5e668f8679db56d2d7d5257 "Tests whether the polygon is convex."): Returns true if the polygon is convex, possibly with vertices subdividing convex hull edges. Takes $O(n)$ time.
- [`P.asPolygonWithHoles()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#ae4dbc2d7bc8b01702980d8023abddd76 "Returns the polygon as a hole-free region."): Returns the polygon as a hole-free [`PolygonWithHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html "Closed region bounded by one outer simple polygon minus disjoint polygonal holes.") region.
- [`P.untangle()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#ab85503d835bc7afa41dedd1140caa1dc "Makes the polygon simple in place by uncrossing its boundary."): Makes the polygon simple in place. Edges that cross are flipped and when a flip is blocked by collinearity (collinear vertices) the offending vertex is removed. On return [`P.isSimple()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a5e182cf106f6be5ed3fb49c07daf80c6 "Tests whether the polygon is simple (its boundary does not touch or cross itself).") holds. Worst-case complexity is high.

- Other methods: [`area`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#ad4765e3f6390f06a59f25fef4fcb219f "Computes the area of the polygon."), [`asPolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a66107f64a7d5194bb7da8d93d809e8a6 "Returns the polygon as a one-component set of regions."), [`bbox`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a1ff93373098baf44e68ba00bb02565d6 "Computes the bounding box of the polygon."), ### Polygon with Holes

The class template [`PolygonWithHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html "Closed region bounded by one outer simple polygon minus disjoint polygonal holes.") represents a polygon that has a set of disjoint polygonal holes. Let $P$ be the outer polygon and $H_i^\circ$ be the interior of the hole $H_i$. The polygon with holes $A$ is a closed region defined as the outer polygon minus the **interiors** of the holes:

$$A = P \setminus \bigcup_i H_i^\circ.$$

For all $i$, the hole $H_i$ must satisfy $H_i \subseteq P$. Every pair of distinct holes must be interior disjoint, but their boundaries may intersect.

The boundary of $A$ is the union of the boundary of $P$ and the boundary of every hole $H_i$. Notice that $A$ is connected but its interior may not be.

The outer boundary and every hole are ordinary [`Polygon`](#polygon) values, each in [`Polygon`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html "Closed simple polygon stored by its vertices.")'s own canonical form (counterclockwise, lexicographically smallest vertex first) — holes are *not* stored reversed. Equality, ordering and hashing do not depend on the order the holes were given in.

```C++
pgl::Polygon<> outer({0,0, 10,0, 10,10, 0,10});
pgl::Polygon<> hole({4,4, 6,4, 6,6, 4,6});
pgl::PolygonWithHoles<> region(outer, std::vector{hole});
std::cout << region << std::endl;
// Output: PolygonWithHoles[Polygon[(0,0),(10,0),(10,10),(0,10)],Polygon[(4,4),(6,4),(6,6),(4,6)]]
std::cout << region.area() << ' ' << region.holeCount() << ' ' << region.vertexCount();
// Output: 96 1 8
```

As with [`Polygon`](#polygon), whose constructor does not check simplicity, structural validity is a documented precondition rather than an enforced invariant: every polygon must be simple, each hole must lie inside the outer polygon — closed containment, so a hole may touch the outer ring but never pokes out through it — and hole interiors must be pairwise disjoint. The method [`isValid`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#aa97419a7e6b85e7bc47411c68c352131 "Tests the structural contract: every ring simple, every hole inside the outer boundary, hole interiors pairwise disjoint.") checks the whole contract on demand.

A region `A` with $n$ vertices in total and $k$ holes has methods such as:

- [`A.outer()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a8e97c883e94cc3cfea21a199228b9b19 "Returns the outer boundary."): Returns the outer boundary polygon.
- [`A.holeCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a95fa631cdfb182d4582639f27036ad90 "Returns the number of holes.") / [`A.hasHoles()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#af767d2a7dbe8a2b20ce41c5b948a87c2 "Tests whether the region has at least one hole.") / [`A.hole(i)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a2b6447fb67d376262ab25b4dc5a1e8e5 "Accesses a hole by index.") / [`A.holes()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#ae82e3ee3003e31fd957a88a84d3e6ed9 "Returns the holes in canonical order."): The holes, in canonical (sorted) order. Iterating a region iterates its holes.
- [`A.addHole(h)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a765b899d5ff3f411408d7a095df3e0cc "Adds a hole, keeping the canonical order."): Adds a hole, keeping the canonical order. A zero-area ring removes nothing and is ignored.
- [`A.eraseHole(i)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a1e2e6aa41d11353728085b52991ccd6f "Erases the hole at the given index.") / [`A.eraseHole(h)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a1e2e6aa41d11353728085b52991ccd6f "Erases the hole at the given index."): Fills a hole back in, by its index in the canonical order or by the polygon itself, the second returning whether it found one to erase (in $O(\log k)$ comparisons, since the holes are sorted).
- [`A.vertexCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#aff0ca302f8ad610564b09c97b15d1ccc "Returns the total number of vertices over all rings."): Returns the total number of vertices over all rings. Deliberately not named `size`: unlike a polygon's, it counts the outer boundary *and* every hole, and a name shared with a shape whose meaning differs would be a trap in generic code. For the same reason a region has no `operator[]`.
- [`A.vertices()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a37281b937de6d6d9317e52d8467b2cba "Returns the vertices of every ring, outer boundary first.") / [`A.edges()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#ae82fd7c3b3450b695607e85c1508976e "Returns the boundary edges of every ring, outer boundary first."): The vertices and the boundary edges of every ring, outer boundary first.
- [`A.orientedEdges()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a520a035a55a65cbab4f6fd49fb4a38d9 "Returns the boundary edges directed so the region lies to the left."): The boundary edges directed so the region lies to the left: the outer ring counterclockwise as stored, the hole rings **reversed**, i.e. clockwise.
- [`A.empty()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#ad252b967097b7afea60a29f85d59362b "Tests whether the region has no outer boundary at all."): Returns true if the region has no outer boundary at all.
- [`A.isDegenerate()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a19709e1f5fa9a79190dceb0c342c8655 "Tests whether the region has zero area."): Returns true if the region has null area.
- [`A.isPoint()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#aeb77d11dab5d9d07d77c3e5dce5fb7af "Tests whether the region covers exactly one point.") / [`A.isSegment()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a687a023801f7924f547d06206c46d6ac "Tests whether the region covers exactly one segment of positive length."): Whether the region covers exactly one point, or exactly one segment of positive length. Zero-area holes are dropped at construction, so both are decided by the outer boundary alone.
- [`A.isUndefined()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#ad566200cce1c54bd278106b5390b8138 "Tests whether the region is degenerate without covering a point or a segment (which includes the empty region)."): True if the region is degenerate without covering a point or a segment, which includes the empty region.
- [`A.isSimple()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#addbf9b8fc422b3358fa22a07f59629a4 "Tests whether every ring is simple."): Returns true if every ring is simple. This is a per-ring check only and says nothing about how the rings sit relative to one another. Takes $O(n \log n)$ time.
- [`A.isValid()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#aa97419a7e6b85e7bc47411c68c352131 "Tests the structural contract: every ring simple, every hole inside the outer boundary, hole interiors pairwise disjoint."): Tests the whole structural contract above. Takes $O(n \log n)$ time, plus one containment test per hole and one interior-overlap test per bounding-box-overlapping hole pair.
- [`A.isRegular()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a2e05e6ecb46a97c1fb30a652c59baf23 "Tests whether the region is the closure of its own interior (A = closure(A°))."): Returns true if the region is the closure of its own interior, $A = \mathrm{closure}(A^\circ)$. Since the contract above constrains interiors only, a valid region may pinch shut along a whole stretch of edge — a **slit**, region material with no area on either side of it, as when a hole shares an edge with another hole or with the outer boundary. A slit belongs to $A$ but not to $\mathrm{closure}(A^\circ)$, so a region with area is regular exactly when it has no slit. Pinching at an isolated *point* is not a slit: the interior still reaches the point from every side, so rings meeting at a vertex leave the region regular. Takes $O(n^2)$ time.
- [`A.regularized()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a5a58f8d14f3eca262dda7a9cd7b28240 "Returns the region without its slits (closure(A°)), as a set of regions."): Returns $\mathrm{closure}(A^\circ)$ — the region without its slits — as a `std::vector<PolygonWithHoles>`, the same regularization every [boolean operation](shape_methods.md#boolean-operations) applies to its own result. Dropping the slits can disconnect what they were holding together, which is why the result is a set of regions: a region whose slits are its only connective tissue comes back as several pieces, and a region with no area comes back empty. A region that is already regular is returned unchanged, vertex for vertex; the pieces of one that is not are read off an arrangement of its boundary, which drops vertices that no longer sit at a corner.
- [`A.twiceArea()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a72bf7dc635f8ef51741366e50abcd93a "Computes twice the area of the region."): Returns twice the area, `2·area(outer) − Σ 2·area(hole)`, exactly and without division.
- `A.area<ResultNumber>()`: Returns the area; the final division by two is exact by default for integral receivers.
- `A.centroid<ResultNumber>()`: Returns the area-weighted centroid, the holes entering with negative weight. When the net area is zero the region has no area-weighted centroid and the centroid of the vertex set is returned instead.
- `A.verticesCentroid<ResultNumber>()`: Returns the centroid of the vertex set over all rings.
- `A.pointInside<ResultNumber>()`: Returns a point strictly inside the region, so inside the outer boundary and outside every hole. A polygon finds one from an ear of its smallest vertex; that argument does not survive holes — an ear can be occupied by one — so this triangulates, in $O(n \log n)$ time. It may divide coordinates by four and is undefined for a region with no area.
- [`A.triangulation()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#af82e342491cc24b09de583b69c4ef4bf "Builds the constrained Delaunay triangulation of this region."): Returns the constrained Delaunay [triangulation](data_structures.md#triangulation) of the region, optionally with extra interior constraint segments. Every ring becomes constrained edges and the hole interiors are left out of the domain, so the in-domain triangles cover exactly the part of the region that has area — a slit, having none, carries no triangle.
- [`A.diameter()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#ab228725f55c314fc60383ffa2b06adfd "Returns a segment realizing the diameter (the farthest vertex pair).") / [`A.bbox()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a030085f5ccf7e57317823cbb2e742be2 "Computes the bounding box of the region."): The holes lie inside the outer boundary and cannot contribute, so both are the outer polygon's.

Against a region of $n$ vertices and an operand of $m$:

- The predicates against a point take $O(n)$ time, and those against a segment, a line, a ray, or a half-plane take $O(n)$ time as well ([`interiorsIntersect`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a0e60fd32003f784f7856f790aab42f95 "Tests whether the interiors of the shapes intersect (A° ∩ B° ≠ ∅).") adds $O(c^2)$ for the $c$ boundary crossings the operand makes, and against a half-plane it is $O(n)$ when no rings touch and $O(n^3)$ in the worst case).
- The predicates against a bounded shape with area take $O(n \cdot m)$ time, and [`interiorsIntersect`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a0e60fd32003f784f7856f790aab42f95 "Tests whether the interiors of the shapes intersect (A° ∩ B° ≠ ∅).") takes $O(n \log n + n \cdot m)$ when it falls back on the triangulated domain — against another region, where there is no boundary shortcut, $O(n \log n + m \log m + n \cdot m)$.
- The distances take $O(n)$ edge queries: the region is closed, so whenever it misses the other shape the nearest pair is realized on one of its ring edges.
