### Polygon Set

The class template [`PolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html "Set of closed regions with pairwise disjoint interiors.") represents a set of [`PolygonWithHoles`](#polygon-with-holes) components with pairwise disjoint interiors. The point set is simply their union:

$$A = \bigcup_i A_i.$$

This is what the [boolean operations](shape_methods.md#boolean-operations) produce — a difference, union, regularized intersection or symmetric difference can come apart into several pieces — and having it as a shape rather than a `std::vector` is what makes those operations **closed**: a result can be fed straight back in, compared, hashed, drawn, transformed and measured.

```C++
pgl::Polygon<> square({0,0, 10,0, 10,10, 0,10});
pgl::PolygonSet<> holed = square.difference(pgl::Rectangle(3,3,7,7));
std::cout << holed.componentCount() << ' ' << holed.holeCount() << ' ' << holed.area();
// Output: 1 1 84
pgl::PolygonSet<> smaller = holed.difference(pgl::Rectangle(0,0,2,2));  // and again
```

The components are kept sorted by `PolygonWithHoles::operator<=>`, so equality, ordering and hashing do not depend on the order they were given in. A component with no area covers nothing that survives regularization and is dropped, and duplicates are erased. The components are deliberately **not** nested: a component stranded inside another's hole is stored beside it, not within it, which is what the cell engine emits and what a flat set can say.

As with [`Polygon`](#polygon) and [`PolygonWithHoles`](#polygon-with-holes), structural validity is a documented precondition rather than an enforced invariant. A set is valid when every component is, when the component interiors are pairwise disjoint, and when no two components share a stretch of edge — they may meet only at finitely many points. [`isValid`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#ad94e8914ee4c3146da2fa1e862796d97 "Tests the structural contract: every component valid, component interiors pairwise disjoint, no two components sharing a stretch of edge.") checks all three on demand.

That last clause is the one that earns its keep. It is what makes the interior of the set the union of the components' interiors, $A^\circ = \bigcup_i A_i^\circ$, and that identity is what lets a question about the set be answered one component at a time. Two squares glued along an edge would have interior points belonging to neither component's interior, and the componentwise answers would be wrong.

A set `A` with $k$ components and $n$ vertices in total has methods such as:

- [`A.componentCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#ad4d95e2b28c9e5c63373114684cd0354 "Returns the number of components.") / [`A.component(i)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#aa9a5bcd6bc13e3bc2490130482e09839 "Accesses a component by index.") / [`A.components()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a9d7dd4f7e2fc61720d22bea18a399a4f "Returns the components in canonical order."): The components, in canonical (sorted) order. Iterating a set iterates its components. Deliberately not `size` and `operator[]`: `size` counts *defining points* on [`Polygon`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html "Closed simple polygon stored by its vertices."), [`Convex`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html "Closed convex polygon stored by its vertices."), [`Polyline`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html "Open polygonal chain stored in traversal order; may self-intersect.") and [`MonotoneChain`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html "Weakly x-monotone polyline stored by lexicographically sorted vertices."), and a name whose meaning differs per shape is a trap in generic code — the same call [`PolygonWithHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html "Closed region bounded by one outer simple polygon minus disjoint polygonal holes.") made for its holes.
- [`A.addComponent(c)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a3971866dab2b17906e8aa896fe13549a "Adds a component, keeping the canonical order."): Adds a component, keeping the canonical order. One with no area, or one already present, is ignored.
- [`A.eraseComponent(i)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a6e25a7b16ecacf2902e030baaf00d635 "Erases the component at the given index.") / [`A.eraseComponent(c)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a6e25a7b16ecacf2902e030baaf00d635 "Erases the component at the given index."): Drops a component, by its index in the canonical order or by the region itself, the second returning whether it found one to erase (in $O(\log k)$ comparisons, since the components are sorted).
- [`A.vertexCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a735173d08465e2229c3219f0b4e3b911 "Returns the total number of vertices over every ring of every component.") / [`A.vertices()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#ac4f23d3e50e18739d63e89628b89db84 "Returns the vertices of every ring of every component.") / [`A.edges()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a298a259daf38720b5f96351a73b165c8 "Returns the boundary edges of every ring of every component.") / [`A.orientedEdges()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#af59e63185d7dc2a4a02635a917fc3c27 "Returns the boundary edges directed so the set lies to the left."): The totals over every ring of every component, with the same meaning they have on a region.
- [`A.holeCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#ad91325e281eeeb2d893d7e5b1dc2efd8 "Returns the total number of holes over all components.") / [`A.hasHoles()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a62e23d5a9008fe5beac363f92faf254e "Tests whether any component has a hole."): The total number of holes over all components, and whether there are any.
- [`A.empty()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a757f15e99380dfe636b26fe7ad89ac8a "Tests whether the set has no components at all."): Returns true if the set has no components at all.
- [`A.isDegenerate()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#abcafe60ef6f7cdd966a9b1aaf0756c51 "Tests whether the set has zero area.") / [`A.isPoint()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a822d90ec47f0161d021b570be4bdf429 "Tests whether the set covers exactly one point.") / [`A.isSegment()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a5601c2c4e04c62419993cd10171502df "Tests whether the set covers exactly one segment of positive length.") / [`A.isUndefined()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a836c663c9280fc5dc318d0e109521e85 "Tests whether the set is degenerate without covering a point or a segment (which includes the empty set)."): A canonical set drops its zero-area components, so a degenerate set is exactly an empty one; only a set adopted with `trusted` can answer otherwise.
- [`A.isConnected()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a549c618ee865d149f43f6d6549e4cafd "Tests whether the set is connected as a point set."): Returns true if the set is connected as a point set. This is the library's first shape that need not be — two components that never touch are two pieces — and it is what the [cut predicates](shape_methods.md#predicates) ask before dismissing a remover that misses the set.
- [`A.isPinched()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#ad2d4aa1226747fc35ac3abbb8246d7dc "Tests whether two components touch each other anywhere."): Returns true if two components touch each other anywhere. A set whose components stay apart is a disjoint union of closed sets at positive distance, and then every predicate folds componentwise exactly. Memoized.
- [`A.isValid()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#ad94e8914ee4c3146da2fa1e862796d97 "Tests the structural contract: every component valid, component interiors pairwise disjoint, no two components sharing a stretch of edge."): Tests the whole structural contract above.
- [`A.isRegular()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a584f3a51697df72e299f9dc6ee313fe7 "Tests whether the set is the closure of its own interior (A = closure(A°)).") / [`A.regularized()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#ac041adf6d9991773979e2ff9e040dc66 "Returns the set without its slits (closure(A°))."): A set is regular exactly when every component is, since no slit can run between two components. [`regularized()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#ac041adf6d9991773979e2ff9e040dc66 "Returns the set without its slits (closure(A°)).") returns a [`PolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html "Set of closed regions with pairwise disjoint interiors."), so the regularization is idempotent in the type system and not only in the mathematics.
- [`A.twiceArea()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a149a627d143e7b9b3c4a483e5c356f96 "Computes twice the area of the set.") / `A.area<ResultNumber>()`: The sum over the components, which is the area of their union because the interiors are disjoint.
- `A.centroid<ResultNumber>()` / `A.verticesCentroid<ResultNumber>()`: The area-weighted centroid over the components, falling back on the vertex centroid when the total area is zero.
- [`A.diameter()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a42f548b878347ee9ad0b39c9a9c73015 "Returns a segment realizing the diameter (the farthest vertex pair)."): Unlike a region's, this cannot be delegated to any one component — the farthest pair generally has its two ends in different ones. Every hole lies inside its own component's outer ring, so it is the diameter of the outer rings' convex hull.
- [`A.bbox()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#afd8fd6f8dfdb8842dad379ed1a9f6799 "Computes the bounding box of the set."): The union of the components' boxes, cached — unlike a region, which delegates to the box its outer ring already caches.
- `A.pointInside<ResultNumber>()`: A point in the first component's interior.
- [`A.triangulation()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a1a3ddf41a22cf7b71b1f09027eeae314 "Builds the constrained Delaunay triangulation of this set."): The constrained Delaunay [triangulation](data_structures.md#triangulation) of the set, optionally with extra interior constraint segments. Every ring of every component becomes constrained edges; the hole interiors and the gaps between components are left out of the domain.
- [`A.convexPartition()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#aa04736f7b8528549264d4d196e2b17b2 "Cuts this set into convex pieces with disjoint interiors.") / [`A.convexCovering()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a0a635a70c1f93a7e3c74dc30fb7a7344 "Covers this set with a greedily selected set of convex polygons."): As on a region, derived from the triangulation.
- [`A.difference(b)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a3d4fbb4a80de7c9d21561535a1fdc664 "Returns the regularized set difference of the two shapes (A ∖ B).") / [`A.regularizedUnion(b)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a66593afcc991bf4a69ccbf38910ce188 "Returns the regularized union of the two shapes (A ∪ B).") / [`A.regularizedIntersection(b)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a6e310ccd32065dff117c2608f16eafe2 "Returns the regularized intersection of the two shapes (A ∩ B).") / [`A.symmetricDifference(b)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a2de2487fb9345e85afa1b3b9c72ad79f "Returns the regularized symmetric difference of the two shapes (A △ B)."): The four [boolean operations](shape_methods.md#boolean-operations), against every bounded shape with area **and against another [`PolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html "Set of closed regions with pairwise disjoint interiors.")** — which is what closure means. [`difference`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a3d4fbb4a80de7c9d21561535a1fdc664 "Returns the regularized set difference of the two shapes (A ∖ B).") and [`regularizedIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a6e310ccd32065dff117c2608f16eafe2 "Returns the regularized intersection of the two shapes (A ∩ B).") also take an unbounded operand, a [`Halfplane`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html "Closed half-plane defined by an oriented boundary line.") or a [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty."), which they clip to the set's bounding rectangle first.
- `A.minkowskiSum<ResultNumber>(b)`: The [Minkowski sum](shape_methods.md#minkowski-sum), against those same operands plus the ones with no area — a [`Segment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html "Unoriented closed segment between two endpoints plus optional segment label."), an [`OrientedSegment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html "Directed segment preserving source-to-target order plus optional segment label."), a [`Polyline`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html "Open polygonal chain stored in traversal order; may self-intersect.") and a [`MonotoneChain`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html "Weakly x-monotone polyline stored by lexicographically sorted vertices.") — and against another [`PolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html "Set of closed regions with pairwise disjoint interiors."). Each component is summed against the operand and the results are united in one arrangement, since the sum distributes over a union and a set is one. It is the one receiver whose answer needs a set whatever its operands are: components that were apart stay apart unless the operand closes the gap. Either spelling reaches it, as it does for [`regularizedUnion`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a66593afcc991bf4a69ccbf38910ce188 "Returns the regularized union of the two shapes (A ∪ B)."), [`regularizedIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a6e310ccd32065dff117c2608f16eafe2 "Returns the regularized intersection of the two shapes (A ∩ B).") and [`symmetricDifference`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a2de2487fb9345e85afa1b3b9c72ad79f "Returns the regularized symmetric difference of the two shapes (A △ B)."), each of which is symmetric and so is the same call written either way. [`difference`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a3d4fbb4a80de7c9d21561535a1fdc664 "Returns the regularized set difference of the two shapes (A ∖ B).") takes a set on either side too, but the two orders ask different questions rather than reaching one implementation.

Four of the five [predicates](shape_methods.md#predicates) fold over the components: [`intersects`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#aa08eaf0d732cb29a97a9f69f4551cfff "Tests whether this shape and the other shape intersect (A ∩ B ≠ ∅).") and [`interiorsIntersect`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a5ba00723092581dfcc914d10d5a3a052 "Tests whether the interiors of the shapes intersect (A° ∩ B° ≠ ∅).") because $A$ and $A^\circ$ are unions, [`contains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#ab95c068a28f7f28a664b4f8308ec1fba "Tests whether this shape contains the other shape (A ⊇ B).") against a point, and [`interiorContains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a6af4ab5f8dcd3cac2715e92980ba2ee4 "Tests whether this shape's interior contains the other shape (A∖∂A ⊇ B).") against everything — the component interiors are open and pairwise disjoint, so a connected operand inside their union is inside one of them.

[`contains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#ab95c068a28f7f28a664b4f8308ec1fba "Tests whether this shape contains the other shape (A ⊇ B).") and [`boundaryContains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#affc29b801f5b51aaceadaa46a5c5a833 "Tests whether this shape's boundary contains the other shape (∂A ⊇ B).") are the two that do not, and only for a **one-dimensional** operand. Two unit squares meeting corner to corner at the origin contain the segment from $(-1,-1)$ to $(1,1)$ between them, and neither contains it alone. An operand with area cannot be shared that way — the two components would have to meet along an edge, which the contract rules out — so the general machinery is needed exactly for segments and chains, where the operand is split at every component-boundary contact and each piece classified. A set that is not pinched skips even that.

The cut predicates feel the same difference from the other side. [`A.separates(B)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#afffd0e104d8e0af261bf9a469008e599 "Tests whether removing this shape disconnects the other shape (B∖A is disconnected).") asks whether $B \setminus A$ is disconnected, and a set is the first shape for which that can hold without the remover doing anything: two separated components are already two pieces. A single point does cut a set held together only by a pinch, which is something no point can do to a [`PolygonWithHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html "Closed region bounded by one outer simple polygon minus disjoint polygonal holes.").

Distances are a plain minimum over the components, with no caveat at all: the distance to a union is the smallest of the distances.

[`PolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html "Set of closed regions with pairwise disjoint interiors.") is an alternative of the runtime [`Shape`](#polymorphism-with-shape) variant, and the only one whose point set need not be connected. That is what lets a [`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes.")-valued [`intersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a4ef86dffede639db1547b404caf4d075 "Returns the intersection of the two shapes (A ∩ B), empty when they are disjoint.") of two regions survive coming apart: the whole set comes back in one [`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes."), where a result that stays in one piece is still unwrapped to the tighter [`PolygonWithHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html "Closed region bounded by one outer simple polygon minus disjoint polygonal holes."). Drawing one on a [`Canvas`](canvas.md) draws the whole set as a single path over every ring of every component, so it is one element with one style and one title.

- Other methods: [`area`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#ac17f7239d703c2c454cb74d04b6c8e24 "Computes the area of the set."), [`begin`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a5b327a0bd579c6530648d36c9775d6c4 "Returns a constant iterator to the first component."), [`cbegin`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a1b64ddd0bc14b1eb1232fb94acdbaa0c "Returns a constant iterator to the first component."), [`cend`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#acf449966ef0a0cd27c1e5fbce2218993 "Returns a constant iterator past the last component."), [`centroid`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a12413cbfee7708e42aff80fe8177cc10 "Computes the area-weighted centroid of the set."), [`crosses`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#aa3b5ecd159c0393dda024b2d926fb883 "Tests whether the two shapes mutually separate each other (each disconnects the other)."), [`distanceL1`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a299c4c1aef858ffa6b22602a3b9a2b44 "Computes the squared Euclidean distance to the other shape."), [`distanceLInf`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#adde028735b5f0abb57847886ed276f23 "Computes the squared Euclidean distance to the other shape."), [`isSimple`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a0482b932f7f1ef3a8096256c32868280 "Tests whether every ring of every component is simple."), ### Halfplane Intersection

The class template [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty.") represents the intersection of a finite set of closed half-planes: a convex region that, unlike [`Convex`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html "Closed convex polygon stored by its vertices."), may be unbounded (a wedge, a strip, a half-plane, or the whole plane) and may be empty. Its vertices are generally not representable in the coordinate type of the defining half-planes: integer half-planes routinely bound regions with rational vertices, so constructive accessors return ERational coordinates for an integral receiver. An explicit result type such as `k.vertex<pgl::Rational<int64_t>>(i)` is available.

The half-planes are stored sorted counterclockwise by boundary direction, with no redundant half-plane and at most one half-plane per direction. A default-constructed [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty.") is the **whole plane** (the intersection of no half-planes) — the opposite convention of `Convex()`, which is the empty set. It can also be constructed from a range of half-planes, or from a [`Halfplane`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html "Closed half-plane defined by an oriented boundary line."), [`Rectangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html "Axis-aligned rectangle stored by minimum and maximum corners."), [`Triangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html "Closed triangle stored by three vertices."), or [`Convex`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html "Closed convex polygon stored by its vertices.").

A half-plane intersection `k` has methods such as:

- [`k.insert(h)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#ac1856ebc53281385a995a6bdd43461ec "Intersects the region with one more half-plane."): Intersects the region with one more half-plane. The half-plane is discarded (returning false) when it is redundant or undefined (a degenerate half-plane bounds no side, so it carries no constraint); when it empties the region, the region switches to a sticky empty state; otherwise it is stored and the stored half-planes it makes redundant are removed. Amortized $O(\log n)$ comparisons.
- [`k.empty()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a3ab10f66c1f39471b44d03eff527b94d "Returns whether the region is the empty set."), [`k.isPlane()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#afece20a10fa322f6450ad3c4691aefba "Returns whether the region is the whole plane (no half-planes)."), [`k.isBounded()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a79271b52491bf5ce89ab26d5ef574e92 "Returns whether the region is bounded."), [`k.isDegenerate()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a7f912f08d9342e92565a52bab98d4ab7 "Returns whether the region has empty interior (it is empty or lower-dimensional: a line, ray, segment, or point)."): State queries. A degenerate region has empty interior (a line, ray, segment, or point built from touching constraints); it remains fully supported by the predicates.
- [`k.isUndefined()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#afd9d78540622355fb2372912daf7d5bc "Returns whether the region is undefined."): Always `false`: [`insert`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#ac1856ebc53281385a995a6bdd43461ec "Intersects the region with one more half-plane.") ignores undefined half-planes, so every region — empty, degenerate, or full-dimensional — is well defined.
- [`k.isHalfplane()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a42737ebaddd223b85cb5eeeae90d7efd "Returns whether the region is exactly one closed half-plane.") / [`k.getIfHalfplane()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#ab024eed55307be448d59f9870c2895d8 "Returns the half-plane the region equals, if it is one."): Whether the region is exactly one closed half-plane (a single stored constraint), and that half-plane. Exact, no division.
- [`k.isLine()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#aba67ebe6622f720ad8145c2b69c160f6 "Returns whether the region is exactly one line.") / [`k.getIfLine()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#af835640cfefbadfc98801afd49eea473 "Returns the line the region equals, if it is one."): Whether the region is exactly one line, and that line. A degenerate region is a point, segment, ray, or line, and only the line has no vertex, so this needs no coordinate arithmetic. Exact, no division.
- [`k.isPoint()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#aa6ad3d5cfc8d1dba95bfe4361f94071b "Returns whether the region is a single point.") / `k.getIfPoint<ResultNumber>()`: Whether the region is a single point, and that point. The test and the default returned point are exact for an integral region, including when the point is not representable in `NumberType`.
- [`k.isSegment()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a734541a80aca5a06fbe267ae516e961e "Returns whether the region is a segment of positive length.") / `k.getIfSegment<ResultNumber>()`: Whether the region is a segment of positive length, and that segment. The default endpoints are exact for integral constraints.
- [`k.isRay()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#ab9e6c525eb4ceb9fcf4c1d2069ab4320 "Returns whether the region is exactly one ray.") / `k.getIfRay<ResultNumber>()`: Whether the region is a ray, and that ray. The test needs no coordinate arithmetic (a ray is the only unbounded degenerate region with a vertex); the default source is exact for integral constraints.
- Together with [`empty`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a3ab10f66c1f39471b44d03eff527b94d "Returns whether the region is the empty set.") and [`isPlane`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#afece20a10fa322f6450ad3c4691aefba "Returns whether the region is the whole plane (no half-planes).") these name every region a half-plane intersection can be, except a full-dimensional one other than a half-plane.
- `k.vertex<R>(i)`, `k.vertices<R>()`, [`k.vertexCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#aa12330e03c05998ca53a4260cfa2a2e8 "Returns the number of vertices of the region."): The implicit vertices, counterclockwise for bounded regions.
- `k.edge<R>(i)`: The boundary contribution of half-plane `i` as a `std::variant` of [`Segment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html "Unoriented closed segment between two endpoints plus optional segment label."), [`Ray`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html "Half-infinite line starting from one source point plus optional ray label."), or [`Line`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html "Unoriented infinite line.").
- `k.bbox<R>()`, [`k.fbox()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#aed55af0630fb978ad186a3ff06c650eb "Computes the floating-point bounding box of the region."): Bounding box; throws `std::logic_error` when the region is empty or unbounded. With an explicitly integral result type the box is rounded outward so it always encloses the region.
- `k.asConvex<R>()`: The region as a [`Convex`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html "Closed convex polygon stored by its vertices."); throws when unbounded.
- `k.twiceArea<R>()`, `k.area<R>()`, and `k.centroid<R>()`: Measures of a bounded region; they throw when the region is unbounded. Their defaults account for fractional implicit vertices as well as the final area or centroid division.
- [`k.intersection(h)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a5da65ca307d0a84216446524765a7a33 "Returns the intersection of the two shapes (A ∩ B), empty when they are disjoint."): Intersecting with a [`Halfplane`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html "Closed half-plane defined by an oriented boundary line."), [`Rectangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html "Axis-aligned rectangle stored by minimum and maximum corners."), [`Triangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html "Closed triangle stored by three vertices."), [`Convex`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html "Closed convex polygon stored by its vertices."), or another [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty.") returns another [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty."), so the type is closed under these operations and the result is exact (no coordinate divisions).
- [`k.intersection(P)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a5da65ca307d0a84216446524765a7a33 "Returns the intersection of the two shapes (A ∩ B), empty when they are disjoint."): Intersecting with a [`Polygon`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html "Closed simple polygon stored by its vertices.") returns the usual `std::vector` of components — points, polylines, and polygons — since a reflex polygon can meet the convex region in several disjoint pieces. The region is first clipped to the polygon's bounding rectangle, which changes nothing and makes it a convex polygon; a region with empty interior contributes only its carrier, clipped to the polygon. The pieces are cut at crossings of the constraint lines and are generally rational, so an integral receiver returns ERational coordinates by default.
- [`k.minkowskiSum(b)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a9cfb54dfc498773d83a64e1ef024608f "Returns the Minkowski sum of this shape and another (A ⊕ B)."): The [Minkowski sum](shape_methods.md#minkowski-sum) with any unbounded convex shape `b` — a [`Halfplane`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html "Closed half-plane defined by an oriented boundary line."), [`Line`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html "Unoriented infinite line."), [`OrientedLine`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html "Directed infinite line with left/right side semantics plus optional line label."), [`Ray`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html "Half-infinite line starting from one source point plus optional ray label.") or another [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty.") — or any bounded convex one — a [`Segment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html "Unoriented closed segment between two endpoints plus optional segment label."), [`OrientedSegment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html "Directed segment preserving source-to-target order plus optional segment label."), [`Rectangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html "Axis-aligned rectangle stored by minimum and maximum corners."), [`Triangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html "Closed triangle stored by three vertices.") or [`Convex`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html "Closed convex polygon stored by its vertices."). The sum of two convex polyhedra is a convex polyhedron, so the answer is a [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty.") again, bounded exactly when both operands are. It is the one sum returning a single convex shape that leaves the operands' lattice: a region's own vertices are crossings of its boundary lines, so an integral receiver answers in ERational coordinates. Every other pair in that family — including a [`Ray`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html "Half-infinite line starting from one source point plus optional ray label."), [`Line`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html "Unoriented infinite line.") or [`Halfplane`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html "Closed half-plane defined by an oriented boundary line.") against another of those or against a bounded convex shape — keeps the operands' coordinate type. The [region-valued sums](shape_methods.md#minkowski-sum) of a non-convex operand leave the lattice for a different reason, and take a `ResultNumber` to say so. A non-convex operand is not accepted.
- [`k.regularizedIntersection(A)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#aac67155f245f545bd9aa63fc48ad8da3 "Forwards a regularized intersection to the shape that owns it."): Intersecting with a [`PolygonWithHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html "Closed region bounded by one outer simple polygon minus disjoint polygonal holes.") through the regularized region operation returns a [`PolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html "Set of closed regions with pairwise disjoint interiors.") — see [Boolean Operations](shape_methods.md#boolean-operations) — exact whatever the result type, since a holed operand keeps its holes.

A half-plane intersection is also something a bounded shape with area can **remove**: the six shapes the [boolean operations](shape_methods.md#boolean-operations) act on all take `k` as the subtrahend of their own difference, clipping it to the receiver's bounding rectangle first. The result lies inside the receiver, so it is bounded however far `k` reaches. The reverse is not defined: that one is unbounded, and no [`PolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html "Set of closed regions with pairwise disjoint interiors.") can hold it.

If the region has $n$ half-planes, then:

- [`k.contains(p)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a0339b8574bb578ad289a1a023fae4976 "Tests whether this shape contains the other shape (A ⊇ B)."), [`k.intersects(s)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#ad5ce4d362f769f6da4b6e41237f86450 "Tests whether this shape and the other shape intersect (A ∩ B ≠ ∅)."), and the other predicates against points, segments, lines, rays, and half-planes take $O(\log n)$ time ([`separates`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#aac1cadcd51404840ccd7051666626b74 "Tests whether removing this shape disconnects the other shape (B∖A is disconnected).") against a half-plane takes $O(n)$).
- [`k.insert(h)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#ac1856ebc53281385a995a6bdd43461ec "Intersects the region with one more half-plane.") takes $O(\log n)$ amortized comparisons (plus vector element moves).
- [`k.isBounded()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a79271b52491bf5ce89ab26d5ef574e92 "Returns whether the region is bounded.") and [`k.vertexCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#aa12330e03c05998ca53a4260cfa2a2e8 "Returns the number of vertices of the region.") take $O(n)$ time.

Equality compares the stored half-planes: for full-dimensional regions the non-redundant half-planes are a canonical function of the point set, so this is geometric equality; for lower-dimensional (degenerate) regions the representation is not unique and equality is representational.

[`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty.") is an alternative of the polymorphic [`Shape`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Shape.html "Runtime variant wrapper over the supported primitive shapes.") class and can be drawn on a [canvas](canvas.md), which clips the region to the visible viewport and strokes only its real boundary edges. Note that `Shape::get`, `Shape::operator[]`, and `Shape::index` throw for this alternative, since its indexable elements are half-planes rather than points.
